title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 5 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: Which particles move from one object to another when objects are charged by friction?
An object gains electrons. What type of charge does it now have?
Two negatively charged balloons will attract each other.
Static electricity builds up most easily on…
questions.explanation: Charges cannot flow away through an insulator like plastic.

questions.prompt: What is the sound caused by the rapid expansion of air heated by lightning?
Match each pair of objects to the force between them.

pairs.left: A positive rod and a negative rod
A neutral rod and a neutral rod

questions.prompt: Why are fuel tankers earthed with a wire before petrol is pumped out?
questions.memo:
✓ Friction of the flowing fuel can build up static charge (1)
✓ A spark could ignite the petrol vapour; earthing lets the charge flow safely away (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Electric Circuits and Energy Transfer

questions.prompt: Current can flow in a circuit with a gap in it.
questions.explanation: A circuit must be complete (closed) for current to flow.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures electric current?
In what unit is current measured?
What is the main useful energy conversion in an electric motor?
Are the lights in a house wired in series or in parallel?
Match each component to its main energy conversion.
What is a short circuit and why is it dangerous?
questions.memo:
✓ Current flows through a path with very low resistance, bypassing the components (1)
✓ A very large current flows, which makes wires hot and can cause fires / flattens the battery (1)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a luminous object?
What is the splitting of white light into its colours called?

questions.memo:
✓ Black (1)

questions.prompt: Match each galaxy to its type.
About how many minutes does light take to travel from the sun to the Earth?
Explain what astronomers mean when they say that looking at distant galaxies is looking back in time.
questions.memo:
✓ Light takes a very long time (millions of years) to travel from distant galaxies to Earth (1)
